title: Let’s Take a Look at Hunters AD 2114
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HUbRq3GR8SI

Recorded in March 2020 from a Washington State that was among the hardest-hit places in the early pandemic, this is Daniel (@dungeondive) doing something he rarely does: a blind unboxing. Hunters AD 2114 had just arrived from Kickstarter, and he backed it for two reasons. It shipped as a single medium box rather than a tower of expansions, and the pitch read like a science-fiction Kingdom Death crossed with This War of Mine and Horizon Zero Dawn: survivors rebuilding a settlement while hunting giant robot beasts for parts.

Component by component, he is mostly pleased. The 31-page rulebook is a small magazine size that earns his approval, the solo mode runs two survivors, the 60-page mission book holds around sixty scenarios with branching choices, and the item system puts weapons on cardboard chips that physically slot together with ammo and scopes. Hundreds of numbered tarot-sized story, road and town cards impress him most, as does a cyberpunk implant deck that includes a subdermal pocket. The icon-dense reference sheet gives him pause, the tuck boxes feel flimsy, and the dice are hollow-light. He bets, against hope, that the rulebook will not be well written because it is a Kickstarter. The whole thing, he admits, feels a little too much of its moment, and he signs off hoping the world does not turn into this.

----

Daniel backed this partly because it was one box, not a mini-bloated tower. Has Kickstarter scale put you off backing games, or is bigger still better?
